Rewrite other codes for unknown parents and sex into pedkindraw's

Source: R/recodePedigree.R
recodePedigree.Rd

Pedigrees written by other tools often give an unknown parent as 0 or leave it empty, and a sex as 1 and 2 or as a word. recodePedigree() rewrites these into the codes the rest of the package reads: NA for an unknown parent, and "M", "F", "H" and "U" for male, female, hermaphrodite and unknown sex. It changes nothing else, and a pedigree already written in these codes comes back as it was.

Usage

recodePedigree(ped, missingParentCodes = c("0", "NA", ""))

Arguments

ped

a data frame with the columns id, sire and dam, and optionally sex. Factor columns are read by their labels and numbers as text.

missingParentCodes

a character vector of the values that mean an unknown parent, compared with sire and dam as text; by default "0", "NA" and "" (empty or spaces only), the codes checkPedigree reports. character(0) leaves the parents as they are.

Value

ped, with each unknown parent written NA and each sex written "M", "F", "H" or "U" where it was written another way; its other columns, rows and ids unchanged.

Details

Parents

In sire and dam, each value named in missingParentCodes becomes NA; "" there stands for an empty or spaces-only value. A value that is also the id of a row is a real parent and is kept, as checkPedigree reads it. Each column keeps its type, so number ids stay numbers.

Sex

When ped has a sex column, it is returned as text, or as a factor when it is one (its levels rewritten, and levels that become one code merged). Case and spaces around a value are ignored: "M", "male" and 1 become "M"; "F", "female" and 2 become "F"; "H" and "hermaphrodite" become "H"; "U", "unknown", 3 and 4 become "U". An empty or spaces-only value becomes NA, an unrecorded sex, and NA stays NA. Any other value, such as "mael", is left as written, so checkPedigree still reports it.

The numbers 1 and 2 are read as nprcgenekeepr's convertSexCodes(), kinship2's pedigree() and Pedixplorer read them, and 3 and 4 as convertSexCodes() reads them by default (kinship2 reads 4 as a terminated pregnancy, which asPedFrame also writes as "U"). Unlike convertSexCodes(), recodePedigree() keeps "H", NA and any value it does not know.

See also

checkPedigree, asPedFrame

Examples

## A pedigree written as kinship2's sample data write theirs.
ped <- data.frame(
  id = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
  sire = c("0", "0", "A", "A"),
  dam = c("0", "0", "B", "B"),
  sex = c("male", "female", "1", "2")
)
checkPedigree(ped)
#>                check id                    detail
#> 1 missingParentCodes  0 sire of A, B; dam of A, B
#> 2           sexCodes  A       sex "male" in row 1
#> 3           sexCodes  B     sex "female" in row 2
#> 4           sexCodes  C          sex "1" in row 3
#> 5           sexCodes  D          sex "2" in row 4
recoded <- recodePedigree(ped)
recoded
#>   id sire  dam sex
#> 1  A <NA> <NA>   M
#> 2  B <NA> <NA>   F
#> 3  C    A    B   M
#> 4  D    A    B   F
checkPedigree(recoded)
#> [1] check  id     detail
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
findGeneration(recoded$id, recoded$sire, recoded$dam)
#> [1] 0 0 1 1
